spiritual_reading:
The Divine disclosed wisdom that had been hidden, and by that disclosure formed a full understanding in those who were being taught. He set forth the primal truth that all things begin from the Divine utterance, and that the whole work of regeneration is a separation of what is from heaven from what is from hell. By influx from higher degrees into lower degrees, truths were extended and arranged in order, until the time when opposition would rise and contend for dominion. Yet above all those contests there remained the uncreated wisdom itself, pure and unmingled, in which no falsity can dwell.

From the perverted will and understanding arose denial of good and truth, and with it the outward life of that denial. This denial took its origin from a first principle of separation from the Divine, and poured itself forth into the lowest degree, filling it with obscurity. In that state falsity was at the greatest distance from wisdom.

This is the first instruction concerning what is everlasting: that each distinct level of life exists in its own permanence, and that they are distinguished from one another by the degree in which they receive the Divine. The essential point is that falsity made war against wisdom, longing to rule within what did not belong to it. It cast dissension into the ordered faculties, troubled the arrangements of truth, and rose up when the whole was in severe distress.

Then protective Divine power proceeded forth as the first combatting good, engaging the assault directly. It invested itself with Divine truth in its outermost strength, met all hostility, and fixed the opposing force in a state where it could no longer freely act. By that same invested truth it bound the enmity, so that what sought dominion was held under restraint.

Afterwards the Divine established a central governing clarity for the sake of order, and gathered and disposed the communities of living truths. The Divine Spirit of life extended the whole framework of the lower degree, and from the first distinguished what could be elevated from what must be held apart. It provided outer forms of truth for what was to be ordered, and assigned to each its function. It arranged the successive cycles of states in the higher degree, so that through their orderly alternations they might draw off and weaken what belonged to falsity. Thus the structure was made firm and fixed, and the whole foundation of the ordered life was set up.

In the lowest degree, all things were held beneath the higher; and also above, the degrees were conjoined so that influx could proceed without break. The outward level was enclosed and guarded by complete boundaries in ultimates and by a sufficient set of containing forms, so that general knowledges and fixed principles might hold everything in place. The whole established order stood as a firm restraint upon evil powers, lest what is from heaven be forced into mixture with what is from hell.

Then the Divine mediation descended as a third proceeding, and by the presence of Divine truth in a form accommodated to reception, it purified what could be saved. In this way it became deliverance for all that could be restored to order.

For throughout the whole ordered framework, love burns as the active force of life; and whatever is impure is consumed and removed from what is capable of receiving heaven. Thus whatever of truth and good is liberated is purified and is elevated back into its own proper life. Conversely, whatever falsity remains in the outward level is drawn out from what is living, gathered into a fixed restraint, and held bound in its own lot. Then the purified goods and truths enter into conjunction with the Divine, becoming a grateful spiritual delight established in permanence. So the whole comes under one Divine rule, above every level and within every level. From that state there is no longer any opposing principle that can contend against the Divine love and wisdom that reign.

Yet in the earliest states, before the work is completed, these opposites appear together in the same arena of life, and for a time are mingled and conjoined in the outward degree.

This is a first great lesson: that the one who lives in the outward life experiences it as a complex way because of the fullness of arranged truths that should govern it; and because of the many openings by which influences enter into thought and affection, in the various communities and habitual states within a person. Therefore the whole outward life is a field of trial in completeness, touching every aspect of the natural mind. For the Divine itself undergoes labor in the process of restoration, bearing what must be endured so that the person may be delivered. The perception of this, even in part, is enough for one who is willing to be made wise.

assessment: Most lacunae are recoverable at the level of correspondential structure (source of Light, discrete degrees, war of Darkness, First Man as first resisting power, Living Spirit ordering cycles, enclosure to prevent mixture, Third Ambassador purifying, final unopposed rule, early mingling, and the ‘first great lesson’ about the outward life). Exact surface wording remains uncertain in several places (especially ¶1-2 and ¶6, ¶8-12), but the required cosmological functions tightly constrain the semantic content; restorations therefore aim for oldest-layer impersonal cosmological register rather than later devotional or institutional phrasing.
